items.item: A functional dependency X → Y means each X value is associated with precisely one Y value

at.step: Reveal: what a functional dependency actually is

items.item: A candidate key is a minimal set of attributes that functionally determine all attributes in a relation

at.step: Reveal: candidate keys, from the closure

items.item: The closure of a set of attributes is the set of attributes determinable from it via its functional dependencies

at.step: Reveal: attribute closure, computed

items.item: Splitting a relation on a functional dependency's attributes (Heath's theorem) guarantees a lossless join decomposition

at.step: Reveal: lossless decomposition, and Heath's theorem

items.item: Insertion, update and deletion anomalies are the named failure modes an unnormalized schema is prone to

at.step: Reveal: this topic's own measured anomaly

items.item: Most third-normal-form relations are free of insertion, update and deletion anomalies

at.step: Reveal: first through third normal form

items.item: A relation is in Boyce-Codd normal form iff for every FD X → Y, either the FD is trivial or X is a superkey

at.step: Reveal: Boyce-Codd normal form, the stricter cut

items.item: Boyce-Codd normal form is strictly stronger than third normal form: every BCNF relation is in 3NF, but not every 3NF relation is in BCNF

at.step: Reveal: Boyce-Codd normal form, the stricter cut

items.item: Fourth normal form concerns multivalued dependencies, a more general kind of dependency than functional dependencies

at.step: Reveal: fourth normal form, for multivalued dependencies

items.item: A functional dependency is a special case of multivalued dependency: every x determines exactly one y, never more than one
